h1:
Where to stay in
Night Bazaar (Chang Khlan)
intro: Chang Khlan's Night Bazaar is the area most first-time visitors to Chiang Mai pick, because it sits halfway between the old city walls and the Ping River. A few minutes on foot takes you to the night market, restaurants, rooftop bars, and massage shops that stay open late. The hotels here cluster along Chang Khlan Road and Loi Kroh Road, ranging from small guesthouses to riverside 5-stars, with big price gaps even though they're all within walking distance. The trade-off is evening crowds and traffic, and rooms facing the street can catch market noise, so ask for an inner or higher-floor room if you want quiet.

blocks.html: Short answer: The Night Bazaar strip on Chang Khlan Road is a night-market belt between the Old City and the Ping River, with restaurants, massage shops, and souvenir stalls right at your door. Hotels of every tier sit within the same short walk, from guesthouses around ฿900 to riverside 5-stars in the several-thousand range. It suits first-timers who want convenience and food close at hand.

blocks.text: Recommended hotels in Night Bazaar (Chang Khlan)

items.name: Night Bazaar Inn
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · closest to the market · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small hotel of around 50 rooms in the middle of Chang Khlan Road; step out the door and you're at the night market within a few paces. It has a Lanna-style restaurant, a pool, and a free airport shuttle. Rooms are plain but clean and good value. Reviews praise the location, though some note street-facing rooms catch market noise in the evening, and the pool has been closed for cleaning at times. Ask for an inner room for more quiet.

items.name: Royal Peninsula Hotel Chiangmai
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Value · has a pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A budget-friendly 4-star between Tha Phae Gate and the Night Bazaar, about a 6-minute walk to the market. Its draw is a reasonably spacious room plus a pool for often under $30 a night. Reviews call it clean, with friendly staff and easy walking access to everything. A good fit for travellers on a budget who still want a pool and somewhere to sit.

items.name: Duangtawan Hotel Chiang Mai
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Families · big full-service hotel · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A large hotel on Loi Kroh Road, about a 5-minute walk to the Night Bazaar, with an outdoor pool, sauna, jacuzzi, spa, and several in-house restaurants. It works well for families who want everything in one place. Reviews agree the building and rooms feel somewhat dated, but rooms are spacious and clean, and it's good value next to other 4-stars in the area.

items.name: Imm Hotel Thaphae Chiang Mai
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Couples · between Tha Phae and the market · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A design-led hotel sitting between Tha Phae Gate and the Night Bazaar, about a 5-10 minute walk to the market. Rooms are clean and larger than you'd expect at this price, and staff are courteous. Reviews praise the location for easy access into the old city. Some note the building's tall central atrium with rooms around it looks unusual, and breakfast choices are limited.

items.name: Meliá Chiang Mai
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: City views · sleek newer hotel · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A high-rise 5-star on Charoen Prathet Road that opened around 2022, about a 4-5 minute walk to the Night Bazaar. Its strengths are modern rooms, an outdoor pool, a spa, and city and Doi Suthep views from the upper floors. Reviews score the location as high as 9.3 and praise quiet, clean rooms with helpful staff. A good match for travellers who want a new hotel right by the market while keeping calm in the room.

items.name: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Central Chang Khlan · spacious rooms · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 383-room 5-star on Chang Khlan Road, formerly Le Meridien and now rebranded under Marriott, sitting right in the heart of the market belt; a few minutes' walk from the lift puts you at the Night Bazaar. It has a spa, a pool, and several restaurants. Reviews praise the attentive service and spacious, modern rooms; some say it's pricier than local options and note occasional maintenance issues.

items.name: Anantara Chiang Mai Resort
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Riverside luxury · quiet retreat · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A luxury resort on the Ping River, about 0.7 km (a 10-minute walk) from the Night Bazaar, with a calmer, more private feel than the market side. It has a riverside pool, a spa, and a restaurant ranked among the city's best. It's the priciest pick here, best for travellers who want riverside luxury while still being able to walk to the market, rather than those watching the budget or wanting to be in the thick of the buzz.

faq.q: Is the Night Bazaar area noisy, and can you sleep well there?
faq.a: In the evening the area is crowded with noise from the market and restaurants, and rooms facing Chang Khlan or Loi Kroh can catch some of it, though most stalls wind down around 10-11 pm. For quiet, ask for an inner or higher-floor room. Larger hotels like Meliá or the Marriott insulate sound better than small guesthouses, and riverside Anantara is the quietest of this group.

faq.q: How far is the Old City and Tha Phae Gate from the Night Bazaar?
faq.a: Not far. Chang Khlan Road runs parallel to the old city, and it's about a 10-15 minute walk from the market belt to Tha Phae Gate, or a few minutes by songthaew or Grab. Hotels like Imm Thaphae and Royal Peninsula sit closer to the Tha Phae side, so they're a bit handier for walking into the old city than properties further toward the river.

faq.q: Who is the Night Bazaar good for, and who should pick another area?
faq.a: It suits first-time visitors, couples, and families who want food and massage shops close by, with hotels at every tier within one walkable stretch. Travellers who want the quiet, temple-lined feel of the Old City, or the hip café scene of Nimman, may prefer those areas instead, since the Night Bazaar is built around evening buzz and shopping.
